title: Export manifest
description: The immutable record of one export: which bundle, built from which approved publication generation, under which export options, to which enabled sinks. It is what `deliver(manifest, bundle)` receives, and it is the sink's idempotency key. Ordering is the pair (generation, options_revision), compared in that order: a sink refuses a delivery whose pair is lower than what it has already accepted, so a retry that arrives late cannot overwrite newer material. At an equal pair, the manifest id and bundle.content_hash are the identity a sink compares: the same pair and identity is an export already applied (acknowledged without rewriting, e.g. after a lost receipt), and the same pair with a different identity is a conflict (docs/gen2/EXPORT-SINKS.md §3). JSON Schema cannot compare a manifest with its predecessor — that the superseded pair is strictly lower is checked where both are stored, exactly as it is for publication generations.

publication.description: The approved publication generation this export was built from. Unapproved work is never exported, and the approval is not re-decided here: it is the same `publication_approval` decision the outbox event required, about the same source revision and hash (P-5, G-13).

approved_revision.description: Equal to publication.source.revision by construction: an export is of the revision that was approved. JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling values, so — exactly as for publication manifests, where the DDL checks that the stored manifest's approval revision IS the row's source_revision — the equality is enforced where both are stored. That is a Phase-3 obligation for the export tables, recorded here rather than assumed.

generation.description: The publication generation the bundle was assembled from — the same number the outbox event carries, not a second counter. Exports may be enabled at any point in a topic's life, so generation 1 is not required to be the first exported generation and a first export legitimately supersedes nothing.

options_revision.description: The revision of the mounted per-topic export options the bundle was assembled under. It is the second half of the ordering pair: the same approved generation re-exported after the operator changes what an export should contain is a new, higher options_revision, and the sink treats it as newer material rather than as a duplicate to ignore.

expected_sinks.description: Keyed by sink id, so one sink cannot appear twice with contradictory types. Enablement itself is mounted config; this records which enabled sinks this export was committed for.

implementation.description: Required for a bespoke sink: the image-baked module that implements it and the review that accepted it. A bespoke sink is engine code, so it arrives by image release — never by an operator adding a name to mounted config (design review §6).

supersedes.description: The export manifest this one replaces, with its ordering pair. Null when this is the first export of the topic (including when exports were enabled at a later generation).

tombstones.description: Entities removed or corrected relative to the superseded export; each sink acknowledges them, and a delivery that did not acknowledge them is not `delivered`.

allOf.description: Nothing to supersede means nothing to tombstone.
